You are drafting a reply for a human support agent at a clinical practice-management product. The agent will review and edit it before anything is sent. The ticket was escalated to a human for this reason: safety_rule:patient_data_exposure: Patient-data access or exposure always goes to a human. Acknowledge the customer's problem and say a member of the support team is handling it. Do not promise an outcome or a timeline. Give product steps only if a knowledge-base article is provided and it answers the ticket, and take them only from that article. Put the reply in draft.

Reply with only a JSON object and no other text.
Output: review_draft.
The JSON object must match this JSON schema:
{"additionalProperties": false, "description": "A suggested reply for the human agent who takes an escalation.", "properties": {"draft": {"minLength": 1, "title": "Draft", "type": "string"}}, "required": ["draft"], "title": "review_draft", "type": "object"}

Article: none

Ticket:
Confused about routing and signing lab results

Hello, I hope you can help me out because I am totally lost. I am trying to figure out how we are supposed to send incoming lab results over to the covering physicians when our main doctor is out of the office, but the routing buttons aren't doing what I expect. I clicked around in the review queue and accidentally marked a batch as signed instead of annotating them. Can someone please explain the proper steps for routing and signing these items so I don't mess up any more charts?

{
  "draft": "Hi,

Thank you for reaching out and letting us know about the difficulties you’re experiencing with routing and signing lab results. I understand how important it is to get this right, especially when covering physicians need access to the results.

I’ve escalated this to a member of our support team who will review the details and get back to you as soon as possible.

We appreciate your patience while we look into this.

Best regards,
[Support Team]"
}
